title: Custom Bevel Gears - UAlberta FSAE
summary: Engineered a custom 1:1 bevel gear transmission using parametric CAD modelling, gear geometry calculations, and assembly validation for CNC manufacturing.
description: Engineered a custom 1:1 bevel gear transmission using parametric CAD modelling, gear geometry calculations, and assembly validation for CNC manufacturing.
objectives: Redesign the steering gearbox to achieve a 1:1 gear ratio across a 45° shaft angle, improving driver feedback and steering response while maintaining compatibility with the existing shafts and housing.
contributions: Developed a fully parametric bevel gear model in SolidWorks using standard gear geometry equations, allowing tooth count, pitch angles, and tooth profiles to be adjusted systematically.
Selected a 20-tooth configuration as a compromise between the previous 16- and 24-tooth gears, balancing tooth strength, geometry, and packaging constraints.
Designed the replacement gear pair to integrate with the existing steering assembly and prepared the final CAD geometry for CNC manufacturing.

process.title: Gear Geometry & Parametric Modelling
process.body: Derived the bevel gear geometry for a 45° shaft intersection with a 1:1 transmission ratio, resulting in equal pitch-cone angles of 22.5°. Built the tooth profiles parametrically in SolidWorks using a 20° pressure angle, allowing key dimensions to be driven by equations rather than manually adjusted.

process.title: Tooth Profile Optimization
process.body: Evaluated the previous 16- and 24-tooth configurations and selected a matching 20-tooth gear pair to balance tooth strength and compactness while reducing the risk of undercut. Derived the tooth-space taper from the pitch-cone geometry, incorporating a 1.5° draft to account for the changing tooth dimensions between the large and small ends.

process.title: Assembly Validation & Manufacturing
process.body: Assembled the gears in SolidWorks using shaft-axis mates and mechanical gear-ratio constraints to verify alignment, correct rotational relationships, and nominal tooth engagement. Checked compatibility with the existing housing and shaft interfaces before finalizing the CAD models for CNC machining by a team sponsor.

results: Completed a fully parametric, manufacturing-ready CAD model of the replacement bevel gear pair for the existing steering gearbox.
Achieved the intended 1:1 transmission geometry across a 45° shaft angle while retaining compatibility with the original mechanical assembly.
Validated the intended kinematic relationship and nominal gear engagement in SolidWorks, then delivered the final designs to a team sponsor for CNC machining.
lessons: This project strengthened my understanding of bevel gear geometry, parametric CAD, and designing around existing mechanical interfaces. It highlighted the importance of deriving tooth geometry from pitch-cone relationships and validating assembly constraints before manufacturing. Physical testing after machining will be needed to evaluate backlash, contact patterns, and steering feel under load.
